site.title: Chiang Mai Enduro Riders Tracks
site.subtitle: Beginner-friendly enduro GPX routes around Chiang Mai
site.restricted: Please ride these community tracks instead of Doi Suthep or Hang Dong, which are restricted areas.
site.contribute: Found a change on a track? Open the track and use "Send it to us".

sections.title: Easy Enduro
sections.intro: Easy GPS tracks for beginners. All are outside national parks and not restricted, except the Mae Khanin river loop, which is closed during smoke season.

sections.title: Adventure
sections.intro: Longer rides on small village roads, mostly concrete with some dirt, through remote hill-tribe villages. Plan a full day.

items: Proper enduro bike, 150kg or less (anything heavier at your own risk).
100% enduro tyres (not the stock 50/50!), better if with rim locks (to lower pressure if you get stuck).
Full protection: tall enduro boots, knees, elbows, gloves, and helmet. Roost guard highly recommended.
Supplies: full tank of gas, 4 liters of water minimum, snacks.
easy-ish, more technical, but still beginner-friendly.
intermediate, you need significant technical riding experience, don’t ride this alone.

rules.text: Wet conditions: rule of thumb is to always add 1 level of difficulty when terrain is wet. Read the descriptions.

tracks.name: Mae Rim North
fields: Easy track passing through farms and nice rice paddies.
might get slippery on some dirt sections, but no major difficulties.

tracks.name: Ban Thi Doi Ngum Lamphun
fields: Single and double track are flowy and fun. At km 18 and km 25, there are 2 nice reservoirs for breaks. Towards the end, there is a long-ish paved twisty section, going up a mountain with a viewpoint.
40% paved (twisty mountain), 30% double (easy, dirt), 30% single (easy-medium dirt, gravel).
decent traction, some dirt, but no pig skin (laterite).
mostly flat, only one uphill/downhill section on paved.

tracks.name: Hang Dong Mae Khanin river loop
fields: if wet, beware of the slippery downhill section from km 3 to km 5.8 (pig skin, laterite). A beautiful Hmong valley with farms at km 14.4. Then 40+ easy-to-medium river crossings starting at km 21.
50% paved (tarmac, nice and twisty), 50% double (dirt, rivers).
potentially problematic. 3km of a very slippery downhill section with pig skin (laterite). And during the rainy season, the rivers might be uncrossable (depending on the water level).
mostly flat, with a couple of gentle up/downhills.
river section (from km 20 to km 30) is closed during smoke season, so you might be stopped by rangers.

tracks.name: Red Sands
fields: Starts on road, passing through a gated community (ok to cross the gate). At km 17, stop at the watch tower, which you can climb (but be careful as it shakes a lot - not more than 2 people at a time). At km 47, there is a nice lake, a good spot for a break. Avoid detours to the sticky waterfall - too touristy. At km 72, you will pass the red sands playground - stop there to have fun jumping the small hills. The track ends on a nice viewpoint.

tracks.name: Mae Rim West river and mountain temple
fields: The route starts and finishes on a fun, all-season double track with 10+ stream crossings. The middle section takes you to the beautiful Wat Phra Putthabat Si Roi temple complex on easy double track and concrete roads. The return follows a wide, winding asphalt road, then a proper double track and a more challenging single track descent, before repeating the river track back to the start.
45% double track (easy to medium dirt), 45% paved, 5% single track (medium)
Medium, laterite territory. The river section is fairly flat and fun when wet, but the single track and the long double track to the temple get slippery.
The first half is flat; the rest has some steep sections but mostly gentle gradients.

tracks.name: Chiang Mai to Pai
fields: This is a much more fun (but much longer) way to go to Pai by taking small village roads (mostly concrete with some offroad). The track passes through several hill-tribe villages and has beautiful vistas. But there is one (short-ish) challenging section (single up/down hill with deep ruts), were you might need assistance. The track will take you a full day of riding even at a good pace, so start early.
5% single (intermediate uphill), 25% double (easy-medium dirt), 40% concrete, 30% tarmac.

problematic because the short technical section can get slippery and difficult. Also, towards the end there is a river crossing, which might be difficult if the river swells with rain. Don't ride this track alone.
one intermediate technical up/downhill section with ruts.
